I have farmed this small piece of land since I was a young girl, and I know what works here in the South East where the rains come well. I never went to school and I do not have money to buy chemical fertilizer or those expensive new seeds from the agro-dealer, so I keep my own cassava cuttings and yam setts from last season and add compost and plant remains to the soil. My children and grandchildren help me with the planting, weeding, and harvest, so I do not need to pay strangers to work. We do not spray chemicals because these root crops do not suffer much from pests, and the rain God provides is enough.
